title: Scaling Agents on Kubernetes with acpx and ACP — Onur Solmaz, OpenClaw
talk_summary: Onur Solmaz describes acpx, a CLI/workflow engine that drives Codex/Claude sessions over the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) to automate mechanical PR triage: intent extraction, conflict resolution, CI fixing, and shallow review-refactor loops with structured JSON output. He also sketches disposable per-task agents on Kubernetes and an open-source orchestrator for dispatching agents to debug production errors.

takeaways.technique: Structured JSON review-refactor loop with human escalation
takeaways.what_they_do: Runs an agent loop that reproduces the bug, judges the refactor, reviews, and emits structured JSON; superficial refactors are auto-applied, fundamental ones are escalated to a human.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I make it output like JSON structured data so I can put it in like an an it's unlike workflow

takeaways.technique: Mechanical PR triage SOP as an explicit workflow
takeaways.what_they_do: Encodes the repetitive PR-handling steps (find intent, judge implementation, check conflicts, make CI pass, address review issues) as a standard operating procedure the agent executes before a human sees the PR.
takeaways.evidence_quote: All this mechanical work by the time the main the PR ends up in front of you, should be resolved ideally

takeaways.technique: ACP as a standard agent-client interface
takeaways.what_they_do: Uses the Agent Client Protocol so any harness (Codex, Claude Code) can be driven through one CLI interface instead of per-model plugins.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If only you could just standardize them under one interface and you just build it once and then you you ship it

takeaways.technique: Disposable per-task agents in Kubernetes pods
takeaways.what_they_do: Spins up a full Kubernetes pod per task so each agent gets a complete computer, accepting the waste as a better abstraction than shared hosts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's actually using like a full Kubernetes pod. Wasteful, but I think it's the better abstraction

takeaways.what_they_do: From Slack, asks an orchestrator to dispatch an agent to debug new production errors, spinning up a pod-backed session per issue.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can ask it to dispatch an agent to debug it, you know, you're like, I'm uh, asking any new bugs after prod release

takeaways.technique: Bounded shallow-refactor loops, not design loops
takeaways.what_they_do: Allows agents to loop on shallow bug-finding and refactors but forbids them from designing, to avoid AI slop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: As long as you're not making it design something, but you're making it uncover shallow bugs that can be easily fixed should be fine
